name: Isolated Anterior Cervical Hypertrichosis

criteria.description: Presence of localized excessive terminal hair growth confined to the anterior cervical region
No associated systemic abnormalities or syndromic features
Onset at birth or early childhood without progression beyond cervical area

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of localized anterior cervical hypertrichosis with absence of systemic involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and exclusionary; no formal diagnostic criteria exist.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized terminal hypertrichosis of anterior cervical region
searchTerms: patch of thick hair on front neck
localized coarse hair on anterior cervical skin
hairy spot on front of neck

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital or early childhood onset of cervical hypertrichosis
searchTerms: neck hair growth from birth or early childhood

common.symptomName: Well-demarcated patch of coarse hair over anterior neck
searchTerms: well-defined patch of coarse neck hair
distinct hairy area on front neck
normal skin aside from hair patch
hair growth that does not worsen

common.symptomName: Normal skin texture underlying hypertrichotic patch
searchTerms: normal skin feel under thick hair
usual skin texture beneath hair patch

occasional.symptomName: Mild cosmetic concern reported by patients or caregivers
Presence of vellus hair surrounding terminal hair patch
searchTerms: fine hair around thick hair patch
thin hairs surrounding dense hair area
mild skin redness near hair roots

rare.symptomName: Associated mild pruritus localized to hypertrichotic area
searchTerms: slight itchiness on thick hair patch

rare.symptomName: Rare reports of familial autosomal dominant inheritance

imaging: Not indicated; no structural abnormalities detected
genetic: No known causative gene identified; rare familial cases suggest possible genetic predisposition
other: Clinical examination revealing localized terminal hair growth without skin changes

distinguishingFeatures: Generalized excessive hair growth involving multiple body areas
Hypertrichosis localized to a nevus or pigmented lesion
Presence of underlying epidermal or melanocytic nevus

redFlags: Rapid progression or spread of hypertrichosis beyond cervical region
Presence of systemic symptoms such as developmental delay or neurological deficits
Associated skin abnormalities such as pigmentation changes or nodules
